messages:
pagerduty-bot: [P1] PagerDuty: INC-2026 fired — gpu-node-az3-45: kernel panic + kubelet NotReady. Trigger: node-exporter heartbeat lost, kubelet notready. Escalation: oncall@eng-sre -> jordan (oncall)

incident-bot: auto-created incident INC-2026, severity=P1, runbook=/runbooks/node-kernel-panic, affected: 1 host (gpu-node-az3-45), possible customer impact: 1st party Dedicated customers in us-east-3. Bridge: https://meet.example/inc-2026

jordan (oncall): acked on PagerDuty. I'm looking. Any immediate customer reports?

luis (support): saw a spike of 503s beginning 02:10 UTC for tenant acme-inc and some increased retries for streaming calls. ~1.4% error rate across requests routed to dedicated capacity in us-east-3.

maya (eng-sre): noted. Jordan — can you kubectl to that node and paste kubelet logs?

jordan (oncall): doing quick checks now.

jordan (oncall): ```
$ kubectl get nodes | grep az3
gpu-node-az3-45   NotReady   3d   v1.26.4
```

jordan (oncall): `kubectl describe node gpu-node-az3-45` shows Kubelet status: KubeletStopped and LastSeen 02:09 UTC. System logs look like kernel oops / panic. Pasting dmesg tail:

jordan (oncall): ```
[  123.456789] ------------[ cut here ]------------
[  123.456790] kernel BUG at drivers/nvme/host/core.c:1042!
[  123.456792] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
[  123.456794] CPU: 2 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/2 Not tainted 5.10.0 #1
[  123.456796] Call Trace:
[  123.456798]  dump_stack+0x45/0x70
[  123.456800]  panic+0x1e5/0x48a
[  123.456802]  ? nvme_ctrlr_fail+0x30/0x30
[  123.456804]  ? nvme_dev_parse+0x10/0x10
```

maya (eng-sre): NVMe-related panic. Could be hardware. Any automated remediation already attempted?

jordan (oncall): PagerDuty attempted auto-remediate: ipmi power-cycle job kicked once but didn't complete (timeout). I'll try to cordon + drain first to move workloads then escalate hardware.

jordan (oncall): ```
$ kubectl cordon gpu-node-az3-45
node/gpu-node-az3-45 cordoned
$ kubectl drain gpu-node-az3-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

jordan (oncall): drain is failing — a few pods are stuck in Terminating, they are gpu-exclusive pods with local checkpoint files. Error: "unable to evict pod due to node affinity/local-storage"

ashley (sre-runbook-bot): runbook note — for stuck GPU pods use prebaked migration hook or escalate to infra for ipmi forced power-cycle if drain stalls > 5m.

ken (infra): I'm on it — checking BMC. ipmi shows host not responding to SOL and sensor data shows NVMe SMART errors. I'll try forced chassis power cycle from OOB.

ken (infra): ```
# ipmitool command I ran
ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.10.45.8 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle
```

jordan (oncall): after ipmi cycle, node rebooted but kernel panic repeated on boot at 02:18 UTC. Reboot loop.

maya (eng-sre): Reboot loop -> mark node unsched and exclude from scheduler, we need to RMA hardware. Migrate any remaining GPU workloads to fallback pool.

jordan (oncall): set node Unsched and added taint: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-az3-45 hardware-failure=true:NoSchedule`

jordan (oncall): migrating affected deployments -> patching nodeSelector to use `gpu-fallback-az3` for Dedicated fallback, triggering rollout for impacted workloads. Notifying customers.

luis (support): messaged acme-inc with incident summary and that we're failing over them to fallback pool; ETA for full recovery unknown. They've acknowledged and asked for updates every 30m.

ken (infra): RMA ticket created with hardware vendor. NVMe controller firmware corrupted; vendor requested node be quarantined. RMA ETA 48-72h.

maya (eng-sre): short-term mitigation: leave node drained + tainted, scale up fallback GPU pool by +2 nodes (from reserve), update routing rule to prefer fallback for affected tenants. Doing that now.

jordan (oncall): increased fallback capacity and updated smart routing policy to divert 100% of acme-inc traffic to fallback pool. Monitoring.

jordan (oncall): current customer impact: acme-inc error rate down to 0.2% (retries still in-flight), overall cluster errors normalized. Monitoring for regressions.

ashley (sre-runbook-bot): incident checklist updated: created INC-2026, attached logs, marked node quarantined, RMA initiated. Next step: postmortem assigned to maya, due in 72h.

maya (eng-sre): handoff — I'll take second shift. Jordan, please summarize actions for oncoming duty: what to monitor, runbook pointers, and whether any manual follow-ups remaining.

jordan (oncall): handoff summary: 1) Node gpu-node-az3-45 had NVMe-induced kernel panic; reboot loop after IPMI cycle. 2) Node cordoned, tainted hardware-failure=true:NoSchedule, drained where possible. 3) Eviction blocked by local-storage on some GPU pods -> migration to fallback pool forced via nodeSelector update and scale-up. 4) Vendor RMA opened (ticket #RMA-7793). 5) Customer acme-inc failover completed, monitoring shows residual retries. Monitor: dedicated routing errors, fallback pool CPU/GPU utilization, vendor RMA updates. Runbooks: /runbooks/node-kernel-panic, /runbooks/gpu-fallback-setup.

maya (eng-sre): thanks — I'll watch the bridge for the next 2 hours and own the postmortem. For now set incident state to "monitoring" and keep channel updated.

jordan (oncall): setting incident state -> monitoring. Leaving sticky note in case of weird regressions. :white_check_mark:

ken (infra): will coordinate part replacement and update RMA ETA in ticket.

luis (support): updating customer acme-inc with current status and expected next update in 30m.

incident-bot: INC-2026 status changed -> monitoring. Assigned to maya (eng-sre) for postmortem.

maya (eng-sre): taking over — thanks all.

jordan (oncall): handing off to maya. I'll be reachable in Slack for 15m if needed.

maya (eng-sre): copy.

(End of thread)
